justice: The complete lack of dedicated sidewalks forces pedestrians and wheelchair users to share the central roadway with vehicles, indicating poor equity in spatial distribution.
The absence of tactile paving or any clear physical boundaries creates an unfair and difficult environment for visually impaired road users.
Haphazardly parked vehicles (such as the red and black cars) on both sides of the street act as physical barriers, severely limiting accessibility for persons with disabilities and older adults.
safety: The lack of physical separation between pedestrian zones and the vehicular roadway significantly increases collision risks for pedestrians, cyclists, and adolescents.
Parked cars along both edges of the street obstruct sightlines, posing a safety hazard for children and teenagers attempting to navigate the area.
The absence of traffic calming measures, marked crosswalks, or clear pedestrian signage compromises the physical safety of all socially vulnerable groups.
livability: The predominance of industrial roll-up doors and large wholesale signage indicates a lack of community-oriented social or leisure venues for older adults and adolescents.
The complete absence of public seating or benches makes the street uninviting and fails to support the resting needs of the elderly.

High, solid walls with painted characters on the right side severely limit ground-floor transparency, reducing social surveillance (eyes on the street) which is critical for the perceived safety of teenagers and pedestrians.
sustainability: The entirely paved asphalt surface lacks any visible stormwater management or permeable infiltration facilities.
A total absence of street trees, vegetation, or green infrastructure fails to mitigate the urban heat island effect.
The lack of public transit stops, shelters, or dedicated bicycle infrastructure does not support or encourage low-carbon travel options.
aesthetics: Monotonous building facades, industrial roll-up doors, and high concrete walls create a harsh, visually unappealing environment.
Randomly parked vehicles and disorganized street edges detract from the overall visual coherence and cleanliness of the streetscape.
The complete lack of greenery, landscaping, or decorative street elements results in a strictly utilitarian visual experience for all road users.
comfort: The absolute lack of street trees or artificial shading structures leaves pedestrians and cyclists fully exposed to the sun, leading to poor thermal comfort in hot weather.
The absence of benches or any public resting facilities negatively impacts the physical comfort of older adults and persons with limited mobility.

The industrial nature of the street, combined with potential commercial vehicle movement and lack of a safe pedestrian refuge, likely induces psychological discomfort and stress for vulnerable groups.
walkability: The absence of a defined, elevated sidewalk forces pedestrians of all ages to walk directly in the main traffic lane.
Parked vehicles and commercial activities spilling into the street create physical obstacles that disrupt route continuity and walking ease.
The lack of pedestrian amenities, such as curb ramps or safe crossing points, makes the walking experience hostile, especially for seniors and children.
bikeability: The absence of dedicated or protected bike lanes forces cyclists to navigate the narrow central path shared with cars and industrial traffic, drastically reducing safety.
The unpredictable movement of vehicles parking or accessing the commercial units creates frequent and dangerous conflict points for cyclists.
There are no visible bicycle parking facilities or lane markings to improve the convenience and feasibility of cycling in this area.
